newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SELLS DEBT-RIDDEN REFINERY FOR 62 MLN LEVS. [corrected 15:28 gmt]
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SELLS DEBT-RIDDEN REFINERY FOR 62 MLN LEVS. [corrected 15:28 gmt]

text.p: Bulgaria's government approved on Thursday the sale of 75 percent in the debt-ridden Plama oil refinery to local oil trader Euroenergy for some 62 million levs, a government official said.
"The government approved the general outlines of Plama refinery sale to Euroenergy," Privatisation Agency director Veselin Blagoev told reporters.
Plama is the second-biggest refinery after Neftochim and supplies 80 percent of the local lubricants market. The refinery stopped production last November due to a lack of cash to buy crude.
"The new owner is expected to invest around 12 billion levs in the refinary in next five years," Blagoev said.

The Pleven-based refinery had been among 64 state firms slated for closure in the government's reform programme agreed with international lending institutions aimed eliminating loss-making enterprises.

The refinery's debts to domestic banks, amount to around $60 million and seven billion levs. The biggest creditors are the Biochim bank, United Bulgarian Bank (UBB), the TSBank and the First Private Bank (FPB), which the central bank sought to bankcrupt through the courts.
However the privatisation deal lacks a clause binding the buyer to negotiate settlement of Plama's debts to the creditors.
Under Bulgarian law the creditors can seek to declare the refinery insolvent through the courts if they fail to agree a debt settlement with the new owner.
The 25-year-old refinery signed an agreement in 1993 with France's Elf Aquitaine to sell lubricating oils for ships.
Eearlier this week the International Monetary Fund postponed crucial funding for Bulgaria until the government completed closures of loss-making state enterprises or their privatisation.
On Tuesday the government approved privatisation of record-high 19 state firms for $42 million. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
